budget.correctionReason: The native-control ledger timestamp preceded the start request and followed a fresh stopped-state check; an additional preceding minute had been double allocated.

wholeFaceBypassControl.status: rejected and cancelled after a preserved prefix
wholeFaceBypassControl.observedFailure: A conservative whole-face visibility bypass retained the raw closed mouth and different face at frame 146, then resumed the edited open mouth/face at 147. This is a visible performance and identity pop.

regionalForegroundComparison.status: narrow local repair study, not accepted as a general workflow
regionalForegroundComparison.timingScope: CPU face preparation/rendering/export work for this diagnostic; 19 new face renders and six explicitly reused frames. Not Viggle or complete Generate latency.
regionalForegroundComparison.appearanceAndGeometry: One fixed front-sheet appearance/canonical geometry, matched-scene expression baseline and continuous pose-bracketed reference XYZ ratios. No nearest-view appearance switching and no final ONNX identity blend in this candidate.
regionalForegroundComparison.visibilityChange: Remove the whole-face hand/visibility bypass when both faces are actually detected. Retain a pixelwise XSeg ceiling, then veto edits over the current native target hand after every facial warp.
regionalForegroundComparison.foregroundCompositor: Gate only the edited residual against the native generated target. Apply a one-pixel hand-mask dilation and 1.5-pixel face-side feather. Original driving-video RGB is not pasted into the target.

causalSeparation.conclusion: The 146-to-147 pop is repaired by removing the whole-face bypass. SAM supplies an independent foreground veto; it did not cause that particular mouth/identity repair.

regionalForegroundComparison.observed: The six inspected stills retain the edited face and source-driven open mouth across 146 and 147. A synchronized 25-frame artifact exists for moving review.
regionalForegroundComparison.audio: Review-only AAC trim for the extracted window, not an audio-packet-identity claim.
limitations: A forehead-hand event is not a complete hand-over-mouth/eyes, leg, car or other-object occlusion evaluation.
Exact classified-mask pixels do not prove complete real-hand segmentation.
The preserved foreground is the native generated target hand, not a recovery of the original driving-video hand pixels or exact gesture timing.
The whole-alpha XSeg ceiling can suppress legitimate jaw/neck support; preservation of the accepted jaw behavior is not proved.
This 25-frame interval does not establish full-video identity, head-turn, cuts or reappearance consistency.

cropperActualRenderAB.status: no clear still-quality winner; temporal quality unproved
cropperActualRenderAB.reference: The same approved in-scene image supplies fixed appearance, canonical geometry, expression baseline and XYZ ratios for both variants.
cropperActualRenderAB.controlledVariable: Only the crop representation changes for the reference, source anchor, current source and current target. The native source is decoded on the frozen 24-fps clock; the 25-fps original is not sought by frame index.
cropperActualRenderAB.observation: The actual face pixels look similar at all three inspected frames, with small placement/shape differences. Lower crop-jitter diagnostics alone are not a realism, likeness or temporal result.

rejectedGeometryAndMaskCandidates.reason: A neutral mouth becomes visibly pursed and smiles are lost at sampled turn frames. Constraining XYZ ratios did not establish reliable separation of anatomy and expression.

rejectedGeometryAndMaskCandidates.decision: not accepted; no clear overall still winner
rejectedGeometryAndMaskCandidates.reason: Smiles remain, but the neutral mouth is slightly pursed and the inspected lighting/likeness gain is modest. No second full clip was rendered from these stills.

rejectedGeometryAndMaskCandidates.coverage: Six mask-only CPU diagnostics, without new face generation
rejectedGeometryAndMaskCandidates.reason: The proxy produces a visible double-chin/diagonal edge. The cache lacks the original pre-ceiling alpha, original aligned edited crop and semantic label maps, so this is not an exact unified-jaw replay or evidence that the split policy succeeds.

localCoreMLComponentStudy.status: component speed and narrow numerical parity only
localCoreMLComponentStudy.motionDeviceCaveat: CPUAndNeuralEngine mode planned all motion operations on CPU. No ANE execution claim is supported; CoreML provider registration is not proof of ANE use.
limitations: The roughly 5.16-fold speedup is for the decoder component, not the full face pipeline, Viggle or complete Generate latency.
Two real frame-12 decoder inputs produce at most one converted RGB-channel-level difference; this is not full-video scene, identity, gaze or temporal parity.
Compute-plan device assignments are planning evidence, not a low-level hardware trace.
Batch-one specialization is an ORT session override; original ONNX files remain unchanged.
The first symbolic-batch attempt was rejected before prediction and is not a successful benchmark.

fixedLivePortraitStudy.status: completed private temporal comparison; not selected and no quality pass
fixedLivePortraitStudy.fixedReferenceRule: One approved in-scene appearance feature and canonical 21-point geometry; scalar scale and source-relative motion. No per-frame reference-identity RGB blending.

originalStills.findings: Source-relative rotation makes some sampled glances more plausible, but the opening mouth is wrongly open. Lip normalization plus stitching can close it while moving the whole face; that global placement change is rejected.

laterBodyStills.findings: A newer native prefix uses its own current hand masks. Lip normalization without stitching avoids the global head shift but does not close the opening mouth. Eye-opening hybrid changes are experimental, not measured gaze accuracy.

mouthAbsoluteRegionalStills.method: Drive the regional LP mouth Y/Z opening correction with the lip retargeter while retaining horizontal expression. Each output has one generated oral cavity; no RGB mouth/identity average.
mouthAbsoluteRegionalStills.observed: The incorrect opening O is closed without the stitcher global-head shift, and the two clear later samples remain closed.

frameZeroFallback.method: Explicit neutral mouth closure under partial occlusion; unvalidated fallback, not measured source performance.

limitations: Opening ratios do not distinguish every phoneme, tongue state, teeth visibility or pucker component.
Closed-mouth stills cannot prove accurate lip sync, jaw dynamics or teeth behavior in a moving clip.
Predicted hidden landmarks from backward crop tracking are not observed facial motion.

existingUpscalerContributionAudit.status: completed read-only paired-media and pinned-code audit
limitations: This is sampled still/contact review, not a new full normal-speed playback review or an identity score.
The exact two uploaded screenshots are not conclusively timestamp-bound to a saved pair; relevant glasses/portrait examples exist but are not claimed identical to every reported defect.

Only final compressed videos are available for these comparisons. The worker deletes its lossless working bridge after verified export, so changes cannot be apportioned exactly between learned restoration, interpolation/color and final encoding from these files alone.
Two additional completed v2upscales use an uploaded edited source, whose exact source asset exists but lacks a direct Remotion job-hash match; they are excluded from the v3Remotion conclusions.
A sharper plausible tooth edge is not evidence of true recovered anatomy. Conversely, an already-blurred base cannot prove that every added fine feature is incorrect.
No general conclusion about Clarity temporal flicker, all cuts or all face poses follows from sparse sample images.
